A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for a fairly general class of algorithms solving SPPs, the communication complexity is governed by the data similarity, and not by the network diameter.
, when local data are similar,  the communication complexity for solving SPPs can be reduced significantly.
, when the local functions are similar, the communication complexity of solving SPPs can be substantially reduced, compared to the case of dissimilar functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the communication complexity of distributed SPPs can be significantly reduced by exploiting data similarities.
the similarity of the local problems can be leveraged to reduce the number of communications needed to solve the global SPP over a network.
the similarity between the local functions can be leveraged for the design of communication-efficient algorithms.
